subject: Permissions matrix proposal for FinEdge — post-call recap

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Permissions matrix proposal for FinEdge — post-call recap

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — appreciate the detailed walk-through, Alyssa and Tom. Per our conversation, attaching an initial draft of the support access permissions matrix and a short summary of how Redwood handles data categories you called out.

High-level recap of commitments from our side:
- PII classification: we will map your field list to our sensitivity tiers and confirm handling rules (masking, redaction, read-only views).
- Data residency: hosted instances available in us-west and eu-west. For FinEdge we recommend us-west region to start; Private/VPC option if you need on-prem residency.
- Retention & logging: configurable retention windows per dataset (default 90 days for logs; customizable), and immutable audit logs for admin actions.
- Support access & break-glass: database read-only sessions for support; break-glass requires 2nd approver, full audit trail, and automatic token expiry.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We will send a permissions matrix that maps Redwood roles to FinEdge roles by EOD tomorrow (attached).
2) FinEdge to confirm which data fields are considered PII/sensitive so we can map retention and masking rules (point person: Alyssa).
3) If procurement needs the SOC2 artifact or evidence checklist, let us know — attaching the SOC2 evidence request template now.

Attachments: redwood-support-access-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 24 KB), soc2-evidence-request.pdf (pdf, 180 KB)

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Permissions matrix proposal for FinEdge — post-call recap

Thanks Vanessa — that recap is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the summary: 
- Data residency: we want logs to remain in-country (US) but are evaluating keeping certain tokenized identifiers in EU for our analytics team. Is hybrid residency supported?
- Break-glass: Can Redwood provide an SLA for break-glass approval timelines? We need an emergency SLA for nights/weekends.
- Retention: for PII we need a default retention of 30 days and ability for legal to request immediate purge on demand.

I'll loop in procurement and compliance (Marta) — we should be able to get you a PII field list by end of week. Also, can you outline what the read-only support session looks like (scope, data visible, typical duration)?

Alyssa King
Head of Platform Security | FinEdge Solutions
alyssa.king@finedge.com | +1 212-555-0099
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa King <alyssa.king@finedge.com>, Tom Becker <t.becker@finedge.com>, Marta Lopez <m.lopez@finedge.com>

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Permissions matrix proposal for FinEdge — post-call recap

Alyssa — great questions, thanks. Quick answers below and I've updated the attached matrix to reflect hybrid residency options and an emergency SLA suggestion.

- Hybrid residency: supported. Our hosting model can keep logs in-region while allowing encrypted, tokenized analytics payloads to be routed to another region. We surface region on each data object and the routing is configurable per-tenant.
- Break-glass SLA: standard response (attempt) within 30 minutes; we can offer a 15-minute emergency SLA as part of a Dedicated or Priority Support add-on. All break-glass events are recorded in an immutable audit log and require two internal approvers before full elevated access is granted.
- Read-only support session: typical scope is query-level access to specific tables/indices for troubleshooting; no plaintext PII is revealed unless explicitly authorized and documented via a break-glass event. Sessions are ephemeral (15–60 minutes) and recorded.

Action items I'm taking now:
- Attach: redwood-support-access-matrix.xlsx v1.1 (highlights: role mappings, allowable actions, session duration limits).
- Coordinate with Rishi to draft a short "break-glass playbook" we can share in the SOW.

If FinEdge can send the PII field list and priority data flows, Neha and I will map retention policies and masking/redaction recommendations and return a final matrix by next Wednesday (2026-12-09).

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Internal note — copying the thread here for clarity. Next internal steps before we send the final SOW appendix:
